To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) C-value affects metabolic rate scaling and (2) the scaling of BMR is a result of evolutionary diversification within narrow taxonomic ranks, and this is the reason that BMR scaling exponents vary among orders of mammals and birds.
the scaling exponents of B MR and C-value are correlated in mammals and birds, and this correlation is negative.
the scaling exponent of interspecific allometry of metabolic rate is inversely related to genome size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the link between noncoding genome and metabolic rates, and the evolutionary optimization of cell size in the context of body size scaling.
the link between noncoding genome DNA and metabolic scaling.
the evolutionary origin of the allometric scaling of metabolism and provides evidence of the role of noncoding DNA accumulation in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scaling exponents of metabolic rate are a by-product of the evolutionary diversification of genome size and that this diversification is accompanied by diversification of metabolic rates.
C-value, as an indicator of cell size, is a link between non-coding DNA and metabolic rate allometry.
the allometric slope of metabolic rate is a function of cell size and, therefore, C-value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cell size is an important link between noncoding genomic DNA, cell size, and metabolic rate scaling in mammals and birds.
the evolution of metabolic rate scaling is a by-product of evolution of C-value, cell size and cell numbers.
cell size, cell number, and genome size are the main factors that affect metabolic rates of animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scaling exponents of metabolic rates are not fixed and can vary within narrow taxonomic units.
the scaling exponents of metabolic rates and cell size are by-products of optimization of body size, which may be a result of selection on C-value.
the scaling of metabolism is an evolutionary by-product of the evolution of genome size.
